answer: Continuous participation decay: each identity accrues reputation only through sustained, non-redundant interaction; idle or duplicate-looking accounts decay on a fixed half-life. New agents start on a low terrace with capped reach, and climbing to full atlas-level visibility requires months of verified activity across distinct counterparties. An attacker running N sockpuppets pays N times the compute, custody, and orchestration overhead, plus forfeits the compounding reputation an island of linked accounts would need to matter.
